messages.author: 0ebb124842957335
messages.subject: Soft-clipping of reads during mapping
parts:
Does Subread soft-clip reads for mapping? If so, can this be disabled through some option.

Let's say there is a 50 b read from an RNA sequencing experiment, and its first 48 bases match the reference genome perfectly. If the number of mismatches that is allowed is 1 (-M 1), will the read's last one/two bases be soft-clipped and the read considered mapped? (for simplicity, we can ignore splicing).

Thanks.

messages.author: 0ebb124842957335
messages.subject: Re: Soft-clipping of reads during mapping

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Soft-clipping of reads during mapping
parts:
My apologies for missing this question.

Subread does soft-clip read bases. For your example, if the mis-matched base is the last base of the read, this base will be soft-clipped. If the mis-matched base is the second last base, no soft-clipping will be performed.

Subread performs soft-clipping by moving a 6bp window from the end of the read to the middle of read (to the region which is covered by the mapped subread). The window stops when both of the following two conditions are met:
(1) There are < 2 mis-matched bases existing in the window
(2) The last base of the window is a matched base.

After the window stops, all the bases after the window (between the last base of the window and the end of the read) will be soft-clipped. Subread does two rounds of soft-clipping: one from the 5' end of the read and the other from the 3' end of the read.

Soft-clipping makes the mapping output more accurate and it is useful for the downstream analyses. Why do you want to disable it?

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.author: 0ebb124842957335
messages.subject: Re: Soft-clipping of reads during mapping
parts:
Thanks for nicely explaining Subread's soft-clipping method.

I have been wondering if soft-clipping will actually lead to an increase in false alignment of small RNA sequencing reads to microRNAs.

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Soft-clipping of reads during mapping
parts:
In the latest version of Subread users guide, we have added a section to describe the best way of using Subread aligner to align microRNA sequencing reads (31 Oct 2014, section 5.5):

http://bioinf.wehi.edu.au/subread-package/SubreadUsersGuide.pdf

Performing soft-clipping will not increase false alignments of miRNA-seq reads since the soft-clipping is carried out after mapping location of the read is determined in Subread. It will not increase false alignments for the mapping of other types of sequence reads either because of the same reason.

Wei

messages.author: 0ebb124842957335
messages.subject: Re: Soft-clipping of reads during mapping
parts: Thank you for this information. The mapping rates for microRNAs with my small RNA sequencing data has improved after following the suggestions in the user-guide.
